title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 84 (Intimation of appointment of receiver or manager)

content.overview: A person who obtains an order appointing a receiver or a person to manage property of a company subject to a charge, or appoints such a person under an instrument, must notify the company and Registrar within thirty days and provide a copy of the order or instrument. On payment of prescribed fees, the Registrar records the particulars in the register of charges. When the appointee ceases to act, notice must also be given to the company and Registrar.
content.glance: A person who obtains an order appointing a receiver or a person to manage property of a company subject to a charge, or appoints such a person under an instrument, must notify the company and Registrar within thirty days and provide a copy of the order or instrument. content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 84 (Intimation of appointment of receiver or manager). If a person obtains an order appointing a receiver of, or a person to manage, property of a company subject to a charge, or appoints such a receiver/person under a power in an instrument, that person must within thirty days from the order or appointment give notice to the company and the Registrar, together with a copy of the order or instrument. On payment of prescribed fees, the Registrar registers particulars of the receiver, person or instrument in the register of charges. When the person appointed under subsection (1) ceases to hold the appointment, that person must give notice to the company and Registrar, and the Registrar registers the notice. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Appointment notice and deadline
sections.body: Where a person obtains an order appointing a receiver or a person to manage property of a company subject to a charge, or appoints such person under a power in an instrument, notice must be given to the company and Registrar within thirty days from the order or appointment, with a copy of the order or instrument.

sections.heading: Registrar registration
sections.body: On payment of prescribed fees, the Registrar registers particulars of the receiver, person or instrument in the register of charges.

sections.heading: Notice on cessation
sections.body: When the person appointed under subsection (1) ceases to hold the appointment, that person must notify the company and Registrar; the Registrar registers the cessation notice.

hypotheticals.question: A person is appointed receiver of property of a company subject to a charge. What section 84 filing steps apply?
hypotheticals.analysis: Within thirty days of the order or appointment, the appointing person must give notice to the company and Registrar and provide a copy of the order or instrument. On payment of prescribed fees, the Registrar records the particulars in the register of charges.

hypotheticals.question: The receiver later ceases to hold the appointment. Is another notice required?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. The appointee must notify the company and Registrar when ceasing to act, and the Registrar registers the cessation notice.

distinctions.title: Appointment notice and charge-creation filing
distinctions.left: Section 84 requires notice of a receiver/manager appointment over charged property and notice when the appointment ceases.
distinctions.right: Section 77 governs registration of charges themselves.

rows.right: The relevant charge-registration period under section 77

misconceptions.trap: Assuming only the company must notify the Registrar of the appointment.
misconceptions.correction: Section 84 places the notice duty on the person who obtains the order or makes the appointment.

misconceptions.trap: Omitting the thirty-day deadline or the copy of the order/instrument.
misconceptions.correction: Notice must be given within thirty days and include a copy of the order or instrument.

misconceptions.trap: Treating cessation of the appointment as requiring no further notice.
misconceptions.correction: Subsection (2) requires notice to the company and Registrar when the appointee ceases to act.
